objectives.label: Take off from San Pedro Bay
Wheels up, floats down, below 95 mph (83 knots)

then.message: Instructor: Catalina water qualification. Wheels are up and wingtip floats are down. Set takeoff power and hold a straight step-taxi run.
Instructor: Let the hull climb onto the step, then ease back near 76 knots. Keep the floats down until clear of the water.
Instructor: Airborne. Retract the floats with F, climb through 500 feet, and fly south to the circuit marker.
Instructor: Turn back over the bay. Wheels stay up; lower the floats with F and slow below 95 mph (83 knots).
Instructor: Cleared to land anywhere on open water. Hold 0-10 degrees nose-up, wings nearly level, and keep the sink rate below 690 feet per minute.

briefing.situation: Catalina Water Qualification. Begin afloat in San Pedro Bay with wheels retracted and wingtip floats deployed. Make a water takeoff, fly the marked circuit, return below 95 mph (83 knots) in the correct water-landing configuration, then touch down wings-level with less than 690 feet per minute of sink. Two Mk 13 torpedoes are the recommended operational loadout, though no weapons release is required for this qualification.

history.text: This fictional qualification is inspired by the U.S. Navy's wartime PBY-5A operating procedures, not a reconstruction of a particular flight. The takeoff and landing gates follow the January 1945 pilot handbook's water-operation guidance; the Leyte setting provides a representative late-war Southwest Pacific operating area.
sources: U.S. Navy, AN 01-5MA-1, Pilot's Handbook of Flight Operating Instructions, Navy Model PBY-5A, revised 20 January 1945: https://aircorpslibrary.com/pilots-flight-operating-instructions-for-pby-5a/

U.S. Navy, AN 01-5MA-2, Handbook of Erection and Maintenance Instructions, Navy Models PBY-5 and PBY-5A, 15 May 1945: https://www.usaf-sig.org/index.php/references/downloads/4-technical-orders/38-type-specific/42-pby-catalina
